angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 584,388 km at 122.01 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.1964 +/- 0.0198 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 122.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.84 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1472 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract): 584,388 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.87 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1472 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5100 +/- 50 K from Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1472 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1472 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1472.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.529, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
